Contains: Special Information for Tax Year 2024 (Act 1 of the Second Extraordinary Session of 2024, top rate 3.9%), residency/domicile definitions, who-must-file thresholds and 'When to File' April 15, 2025 due date, tax-treaty foreign-student taxation language, line-by-line income section (Lines 8-25), Standard Deduction chart ($2,410/$4,820), Personal Tax Credits ($29), Low Income Tax Tables (Rev 09/23/2024) and Regular Income Tax Table (Rev 09/19/2024), mailing addresses, and check-payable instructions.

_strings.@@74e0e92430e9: If any of your income was exempt from federal tax under a treaty: AR does not conform to federal tax treaties, so that income is still taxable to AR — do not carry the federal exclusion onto the state return.
_strings.@@81fbb800e9e1: If any income was exempt from federal tax under a treaty: AR does not conform to federal tax treaties — that income is still taxable to AR.
_strings.@@93686e445836: Treaty conformity — AR does NOT conform to federal tax treaties: income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is STILL taxable by AR. Do not carry a federal treaty exclusion onto the state return. (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state's Internal Revenue Code conformity date and its deduction/credit conformity are separate questions; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Arkansas does NOT conform to federal tax treaty exemptions. Two independent .gov-sourced facts establish this for 2024: (1) The AR1000F return does NOT start from federal adjusted gross income. It builds Arkansas income line-by-line from source documents — Line 8 W-2 wages, Line 10 interest, Line 11 dividends, etc., summed to Line 23 'Total Income' and then to Arkansas AGI on Line 25. Because income is captured from the W-2/source level, a federal treaty exclusion taken on the federal return does NOT carry through. (2) The 2024 instructions state explicitly (Line 22/income section): 'Foreign students who are exempt from federal taxes because of a tax treaty must file and pay tax on all income including non-qualified scholarship or fellowship income. Stipends are taxable.' That is an affirmative requirement to tax treaty-exempt income, equivalent to a treaty add-back. Therefore treaty-exempt income IS re-taxed by Arkansas -> conforms_to_federal_treaties = false.

Code Ann. 26-51-201(d)(1) indexing note (the $94,301–$94,500 range intentionally spans $200). Cross-verified against the 2024 AR1000F and AR1000NR Instructions booklet (https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024_AR1000F_and_AR1000NR_Instructions.pdf): 'Special Information for Tax Year 2024' (Act 1 of the Second Extraordinary Session of 2024 — top rate reduced to 3.9%, retroactive to 1/1/2024), Line 7A/7B Personal Tax Credits ($29), Standard Deduction chart ($2,410/$4,820) and Lines 26–29, pp.24-25 2024 Low Income Tax Tables (Rev 09/23/2024) and pp.26-30 Regular Income Tax Table (Rev 09/19/2024) with 'For $100,001 and over, your tax is $3,811 + 3.9% of the excess over $100,000.'
_strings.@@a36d798e7a94: Child and Dependent Care Credit — Resident taxpayers who paid for the care of a qualifying person (a dependent under age 13, or a spouse/dependent incapable of self-care) so the taxpayer (and spouse, if married) could work or look for work. Mirrors the federal child and dependent care credit (federal Form 2441 mechanics on Form AR2441). Filing status 5 (married filing separately on different returns) generally cannot claim it unless the AR2441 checkbox requirements are met.
_strings.@@b5738ddbd58f: Personal Tax Credit (personal exemption credit) — Every Arkansas individual filer. One credit each for: yourself, spouse, and each dependent; plus extra credit boxes for age 65 or over, '65 Special' (age 65+ not claiming the retirement income exemption on line 18), blind, deaf, and head of household/surviving spouse. Listed in the Personal Tax Credits section of the return.
_strings.@@c19f6ea1de78: Arkansas 2024 Individual Income Tax Forms and Instructions booklet, WHEN TO FILE ('any time after December 31, 2024, but NO LATER THAN April 15, 2025'); a federal extension (Form 4868) extends the Arkansas deadline to file until November 15th, but any tax due must be paid by April 15, 2025

_strings.@@d2bfeebd34d9: State Political Contributions Credit — Any Arkansas taxpayer who made cash contributions by April 15, 2025 to a candidate seeking nomination or election to a PUBLIC (state/local, not federal) office or to the candidate's campaign committee, an approved political action committee, or an organized political party.
_strings.@@e8e025a01522: Credit for Individuals with Developmental Disabilities — Taxpayers who have a dependent (or self) who qualifies with a developmental disability, as certified on Form AR1000-DD (formerly AR1000RC5). Certifications valid on/after January 1, 2022 have no expiration date; the AR1000TC must be submitted yearly, and the AR1000-DD attached the first year the credit is claimed. The credit follows the child and can only be claimed on one tax return per year.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: AR1000F Line 29: "TAX: (Enter tax from tax table)" — the tax on Line 28 ("Subtract Line 27 from Line 25. This is your Net Taxable Income."), per the 2024 AR1000F/AR1000NR Instructions, Tax Computation, Lines 26-29. This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply AR1000F Line 25, 'Adjusted Gross Income (AGI)' — Arkansas AGI, i.e. Line 23 Total Income (built line-by-line from source documents, Lines 8–22: W-2 wages, interest, dividends, etc.; Arkansas does NOT start from federal AGI or federal taxable income) minus Line 24 adjustments (Form AR1000ADJ). The op subtracts the shipped per-status standard deduction (Line 27) to reach Line 28 Net Taxable Income and applies the brackets (the Line 29 tax). If you itemize (Form AR3), the shipped standard deduction is wrong for you — compute Line 27 on the form instead. Test-vector counts are zero by construction: Arkansas ships NO personal/dependent exemption keys (the $29-per-person amounts are CREDITS against tax, AR1000F Lines 7A/7B) — the engine refuses nonzero counts for this state by design. RETROACTIVE 2024 RATE CUT — Act 1 of the Second Extraordinary Session of 2024 (June 2024 special session): 'Marginal Income Tax rates for 2024 have been amended, and the top rate will be reduced to 3.9%' (booklet, Special Information for Tax Year 2024), retroactive to January 1, 2024. The shipped schedule is the FINAL 2024 filing-season version: the 2024 Indexed Tax Brackets document and the booklet tax tables (Low Income Rev 09/23/2024; Regular Rev 09/19/2024) all print the 3.9% top rate. The whole schedule was re-indexed vs 2023: 0% floor to $5,499 (was $5,299), 2% to $10,899, 3% to $15,599, 3.4% to $25,699, 3.9% above (2023 top was 4.7% above $24,999). Arkansas has ONE bracket schedule for every filing status — the published 2024 Indexed Tax Brackets and the tax tables do not vary by status, so all four statuses ship identical brackets. Filing Status 2 (married filing joint) runs the couple's COMBINED Line 28 net taxable income through the same un-widened schedule; Arkansas instead offers Filing Status 4 (married filing separately on the SAME return), where each spouse's own Line 28 income goes through the schedule in a separate column (tax = Line 29(A) + Line 29(B), summed on Line 30) — often less total tax than status 2. This op models a single run of one income through the schedule. Surviving Spouse is a SEPARATE Arkansas status (Filing Status 6) with a $2,410 standard deduction — NOT the $4,820 married-filing-joint amount. The engine maps qualifying surviving spouse to married_filing_jointly, which would wrongly apply $4,820; an Arkansas surviving spouse gets $2,410 (compute as single for the deduction). Table mandate at ALL income levels: AR1000F Line 29 takes the tax from the 2024 tax tables (booklet pp.24-30), which are computed at the MIDPOINT of each income band and rounded to the whole dollar — 'If you use a formula to calculate Arkansas income tax, the results must match the table exactly. The calculations in the table are made at the midpoint of each income level' (2024 Indexed Tax Brackets; worked examples: $75,900–$76,000 band -> $75,950 x .039 - $409.86 = $2,552.19 -> $2,552; $14,800–$14,900 band -> $14,850 x .030 - $218.97 = $226.53 -> $227). Bracket math may differ from the table by a few dollars within a band; the filed form must use the table. CRITICAL — shipped brackets are exact ONLY for net taxable income up to $92,300. From $92,301 to $95,500 the official schedule phases the 3.9% bracket's 'minus adjustment' down from $409.86 to $87.40 in $10-per-$100-band steps (the $94,301–$94,500 range intentionally spans $200 per the Ark. Code Ann. 26-51-201(d)(1) rounding note), and at $95,501+ the tax is 3.9% x net taxable income - $87.40. The shipped bracket math (equivalent to 3.9% x income - $409.86) UNDERSTATES the true tax above $92,300 — by $322.46 once net taxable income reaches $95,501 — so above $92,300 compute from the official schedule/table, not from these brackets. The Regular Income Tax Table's printed top rule — 'For $100,001 and over, your tax is $3,811 + 3.9% of the excess over $100,000' (booklet p.30, Rev 09/19/2024) — equals 3.9% x income - $89.00, while the 2024 Indexed Tax Brackets constant for $95,501+ is $87.40 (3.9% x $100,000 - $87.40 = $3,812.60): a $1.60 divergence, because $3,811 is the midpoint-rounded last table row ($99,901–$100,001: $99,951 x .039 - $87.40 = $3,810.689 -> $3,811). The filed form follows the printed table/formula. The published 'minus adjustment' constants equal the cumulative sum of the prior brackets to the cent ($109.98 = 2% x $5,499 exactly; $218.97 exactly; $281.37 vs exact $281.366; $409.86 vs exact $409.861) — no material rounding divergence, so the shipped marginal brackets reproduce the official formula to within one cent below $92,301. EXEMPTIONS ARE CREDITS IN ARKANSAS — none are shipped: Arkansas has no personal or dependent exemption that reduces income. It gives $29-per-person PERSONAL TAX CREDITS instead (AR1000F Line 7A boxes: yourself, spouse, 65 or over, '65 Special', blind, deaf, head-of-household/surviving-spouse; Line 7B: $29 per dependent; totaled on Line 7C and subtracted from TAX on Line 34). These credits are not modeled by this op. Other nonrefundable credits reduce the computed tax on the form but are NOT modeled: the 'Additional Tax Credit for Qualified Individuals' (up to $60 per individual, 2024 net taxable income up to $26,900, worksheet p.21 R 10/7/2024: $60 at $0–$25,800 declining $5 per $100 band to $0 at $26,901+), the 20%-of-federal-computation Child and Dependent Care Credit (2024 AR2441 line 10 'Multiply line 9 by .20'), the $50/$100 state political contributions credit, and the $500-per-dependent Developmental Disabilities credit (AR1000TC). The 2023 one-time Inflationary Relief Income Tax Credit does NOT exist for 2024. Low Income Tax Table (NOT modeled): full-year residents whose total income from all sources is within the limits may take tax from the 2024 Low Income Tax Table applied to Line 25 AGI with NO deduction on Line 27 ('CAUTION: If you qualify to use a Low-Income Tax Table, enter zero (0) on line 27, column A. The Standard Deduction is already built into the table.'), which yields LESS tax than the shipped math at low incomes — tax is $0 up to $14,265 (single), $20,282 / $24,176 (HoH or Surviving Spouse with 1-or-no / 2-or-more dependents), $24,057 / $28,953 (MFJ with 1-or-no / 2-or-more dependents), and the table is usable up to AGI of $17,000 (single), $24,600 / $28,200 (HoH/SS), $28,300 / $35,100 (MFJ). Married couples must file Status 2 to qualify; filers claiming the active-duty military, employer-sponsored pension, or qualified traditional IRA exclusions do not qualify (unless they elect not to use the exclusion). Standard-deduction gates not modeled: the deduction is capped at income ('If the amount on line 25 is less than the Standard Deduction, enter the amount from line 25 on line 27' — consistent with the engine's max(0, ...)); it 'does not apply to taxpayer's dependent(s)'; itemizers use Form AR3 itemized deductions on Line 27 instead; and for Filing Status 4 or 5, if one spouse itemizes both must itemize (status 5 prorates deductions by both spouses' incomes). Amounts not part of Line 29 bracket math are not modeled: Line 31 lump-sum distribution averaging (Form AR1000TD) and Line 32 additional 10%-of-federal tax on early IRA/retirement distributions (federal Form 5329) are ADDED to reach Line 33 total tax on the form. Round all amounts to the nearest whole dollar on the return (booklet: 'Round all amounts to the nearest dollar. For example, if your Form W-2 shows $10,897.50, round to $10,898') — half-up, matching the engine.
